cards.text: Isaiah, the prophet, has just been talking about a king who will reign in righteousness. Now he opens with a woe aimed at someone who's been wrecking everything and never paying for it. He calls him, "O destroyer never destroyed, O traitor never betrayed!"

cards.question: This destroyer has torn everything up and never been torn up back. What does Isaiah say happens when he's finished destroying?
Isaiah says the traitor who betrayed everyone will never be betrayed himself.

cards.text: Friend, that's the coworker who's been sneaking the last cookie out of the break room box for YEARS. Then one day he opens the box... and somebody beat him to it. Then the voice turns to the LORD in prayer: "O LORD, be gracious to us! We wait for You."

cards.question: In this prayer, the people ask the LORD to be their strength only in time of trouble.

cards.text: Then the prayer turns to the LORD's power. His voice is like thunder, and He rises up.

cards.question: When the LORD rises and His voice thunders, what do the nations do?
All the spoil those nations piled up gets swept away. Isaiah says men sweep over it like a swarm of ___.

cards.text: Then Isaiah looks up. The LORD is exalted, because He lives on high, and from up there He fills His city, Zion.

cards.question: What has the LORD filled Zion with?

cards.text: He'll be the sure foundation for your times, a storehouse of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. A storehouse! Friend, I LIVED in a storehouse once. Takeout menus. Receipts. Warranty cards. Not ONE thing in that drawer ever saved anybody.

cards.question: With the LORD as that kind of storehouse, what does Isaiah call Zion's treasure?

cards.text: Then the picture flips back to right now. Isaiah says their valiant ones cry aloud in the streets. The tough guys are crying, friend. The tough guys.

cards.question: The envoys sent out to make peace are in the streets too. How are they doing?

cards.text: The highways are deserted. Travel has ceased. Empty roads. Nobody honking. Nobody waving the wrong finger. NOBODY.

cards.question: With the roads empty, Isaiah says at least the treaty still holds and the witnesses are honored.

cards.text: Even the land mourns and languishes. Lebanon is ashamed and decayed, and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.

cards.question: The land is mourning. Isaiah says Sharon is like a ___.

cards.text: Things are about as low as they can get. Then the LORD Himself speaks, and three times in a row He starts with the same word: Now.

cards.question: Three times the LORD says "Now." What is He about to do?

cards.text: Then He says, "You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble." Friend, that's me hyping up a giant batch for an HOUR. Mixing. Rolling. Stamping. I open the oven... crumbs. All that work. Crumbs.

cards.question: The LORD says their own breath is a fire that will ___ them.
The LORD says the peoples will be burned to ashes, like thorns cut down and set ablaze.

cards.text: Then the LORD calls out to two groups: you who are far off, and you who are near. He wants both groups to know what He has done.

cards.question: The LORD's call here is only for the people who live near Zion.

cards.text: That hits home. The sinners in Zion are afraid, and trembling grips the ungodly. I bet some of them were shaking harder than a stamper on the edge of a counter.

cards.question: Trembling, the ungodly in Zion ask a question. What do they ask?

answers.text: Who can dwell with a consuming fire
When the enemy will finally leave
Where the nearest city of refuge is

cards.text: And an answer comes. It's the one who walks righteously and speaks with sincerity.

cards.question: The person described here refuses gain from extortion, and his hand never takes a bribe.
This person stops his ___ against murderous plots and shuts his ___ tightly against evil.

cards.text: And that person? He gets to live on the heights. Friend, my last address was the back of a junk drawer, under a takeout menu. This guy gets the HEIGHTS.

cards.question: Up on the heights, what does Isaiah say will be this person's refuge?
The person who walks righteously will still have to worry about his food and water.

cards.text: Now the message turns, and it gets bright. Isaiah tells the listener what their own eyes will see.

cards.question: Isaiah says their eyes will see someone. Who?
Along with the King, their eyes will behold a land that stretches afar.

cards.text: They'll think back on the old terror and ask, "Where is he who tallies? Where is he who weighs? Where is he who counts the towers?" That's the guy who counted every cookie in the box so nobody could sneak one. And one day... he's just GONE.

cards.question: Isaiah says they will still have to deal with the insolent people whose language they can't understand.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says to look upon Zion, the city of their appointed feasts. Jerusalem will be a peaceful pasture, and a tent.

cards.question: Its tent pegs won't be pulled up, and none of its cords will break. Jerusalem will be a tent that does not ___.

cards.text: And there, the Majestic One, our LORD, will be a place of rivers and wide canals for them. The LORD Himself is the river.

cards.question: Galleys with oars and majestic vessels will row and sail on those rivers.

cards.text: Then Isaiah says why they can rest easy: "For the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our King."

cards.question: The LORD is their Judge, their lawgiver and their King. What does Isaiah say He will do for them?

cards.text: "Your ropes are slack; they cannot secure the mast or spread the sail." A ship that can't do the one thing it's built for? Friend, I KNOW that feeling. I was a cookie stamper with blurry stamps.

cards.question: Ropes slack and all, an abundance of spoils still gets divided. Who carries off plunder?

cards.text: And the message ends with the people who live in Zion. Not one of them will say they're sick.

cards.question: What happens to the iniquity of the people who dwell in Zion?

findings.problem: The card says Isaiah 'has just been talking about a king who will reign in righteousness.' That fact comes from Isaiah 32:1, outside the passage, but it has no reference and the card cites only Isaiah 33:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences plus a two-sentence quote: the cookie joke and then the turn to prayer.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'All the spoil those nations piled up' says the nations gathered the spoil. The text only says 'Your spoil, O nations' and leaves open how it became theirs.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'From up there He fills His city' links the LORD dwelling on high to how He fills Zion. Verse 5 states the two facts side by side without connecting them.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: 'Shaking harder than a stamper on the edge of a counter' relies on a backstory detail (cutters wobbling near the counter edge) that this lesson never sets up. A stamper shaking is not an image that clicks instantly.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'The city of Joppa' is a specific named city. The other two answers are general kinds of refuge, so the answers are not the same kind of thing.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.
